_about: The fall of nations and their return. Every fall is kept on a roll that both interfaces read, in every campaign. The return is a rule of the grand campaign only: a country beaten in the field comes back at a month's end, when its capital is in the hands of an alliance member at war with the country that conquered it (or whose conqueror has itself fallen) and no corps at war with that holder stands in the capital or next to it (forts left out): never in the middle of a month's fighting (ruling 229, part 2). 'gap' is how many months must pass after the fall first: it never returns at the end of the month it fell in. The freed country joins its liberator's alliance, is at war with its liberator's enemies, and takes back every province of its own that its new allies hold. 'never' lists countries that do not return (Vichy is a government, not a country: its ground goes back to a freed France). A country annexed outright or divided by treaty does not return either, and nor does anyone in the last act of the grand campaign, when there are no alliances left to join. The League frees only countries that could be members of it. 'army' is what a freed country puts in the field the day it returns: one corps, and one more for every 'perVp' victory points of home ground it has on the map, up to 'most', each of 'divs' divisions of infantry at 'str' strength, 'org' organisation and 'xp' experience. A freed country stands for as long as its capital does: it cannot be brought down again while the capital is in its own side's hands.

finish._note: Finishing the war together (rulings 111 and 115; finish.ts; the grand campaign, never its last act). When an alliance's chief enemy falls (the leader of the other alliance, diplomacy.json 'leaders': Germany for the Allies), every computer-run great power that was at war with it gives notice to each great power its allies are still fighting and it is at peace with, and is at war with it 'notice' months after the fall (the Soviet Union and Japan, three months after Germany's surrender); its staff then presses that war for 'push' months at least, as it does the wars it is in already against the great powers still standing. The same holds for a great power left with no enemy great power of its own standing, whoever it was that fell; one that still has an enemy great power to beat, and has not seen the chief enemy fall, goes on as it was. It holds at every stop of the history dial and never binds the player's own country. Vichy does not outlive Germany: once Germany has fallen and France is free again in its own capital, at that month's end Vichy's ground at home and overseas is France's and its troops answer to France, unless a player is playing it. A freed country takes up again every war it was in when it fell that its liberator's alliance is still fighting: in the month their chief enemy falls, or as it returns if he has fallen already. So nothing here acts before the chief enemy's fall. 'before' true lets Vichy end with a free France in Paris alone, and a freed country take up its old wars as it returns, while the chief enemy still stands.
